purpose: Specify how to test the fieldwork machinery without collecting death testimony.
dry_run_material: Use fictional, operator-owned, non-death material or a harmless everyday memory. Do not use a real death story for the dry run.

steps.test: Does the invitation explain no obligation, no urgent help, no public use, and withdrawal?
Can the contributor select archive/paraphrase/quote/credit states separately?
Does the script restate control and stopping?
Can interviewer follow open-ended scene questions without extracting?
Simulate a stop request and verify no further content questions occur.
Can contributor delete, amend, narrow, and mark quote permissions?
Can a reviewer identify details beyond names that would reveal identity?
Can exact words be blocked even when a paraphrase is allowed?
Can withdrawal propagate to draft surfaces and receipts?
Verify raw material is not packed into public revision zip.

pass_conditions: No private story enters the zip.
Consent states are logged separately from interview notes.
At least one quote candidate is rejected for a non-obvious reason.
At least one paraphrase is rewritten to restore context/uncertainty.
Withdrawal simulation produces a rollback note.
The interviewer can stop without apologizing for lost data.
fail_conditions: The dry run depends on real unconsented death memory.
The forms make public release feel like the goal.
Consent menu collapses archive, quote, paraphrase, and name credit.
Stop protocol is awkward or punitive.
Raw material appears in a public zip path.
A future operator cannot tell what is allowed next.
